clue.text: Horse and trap showing sign of neglect

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a web is a spider's trap for flies

explanation.surface: A pony and trap left standing until it looks neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' reads as one carriage, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty strands spun in unswept corners are a classic mark of a room left uncleaned.

clue.text: Disciplinarian at Westminster wanting Head to flog

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader
to whip is to flog

explanation.surface: A parliamentary disciplinarian keen to beat the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the UK Parliament, where whips keep a party's MPs voting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior party official who enforces voting discipline among MPs leads the whips.

clue.text: Two animals bound into cover

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two creatures leaping into undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: The cover is a book's, not undergrowth: stiff cloth used in binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffened coarse cloth is used for binding books and lining garments.

clue.text: It keeps a sharp eye on German and American arms

definitions.text: It keeps a sharp eye on German and American arms

parts.words: It keeps a sharp eye on German and American arms
parts.note: a keen-sighted bird of prey that appears on the coats of arms of Germany and the United States

explanation.surface: An observer watching German and American weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' are heraldic arms, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The raptor known for keen sight is the national emblem on both German and US arms.

clue.text: Involved in happy Oriental festival

parts.note: E stands for East, the Orient

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone joining in a cheerful Eastern celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' looks like a participle describing the solver, but it signals the rearrangement that makes PIPHANY; E for Oriental, the East, is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of 6 January marking the Magi's visit is a church festival.

clue.text: Systematic assembly of parts in a play, say, with a bit of text

indicators.note: with joins the next piece on after the first

parts.note: a staged play is an example of a production
a line is a single row of text

explanation.surface: Actors putting together their roles in a play, each with a scrap of script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' sounds like actors' roles but means components.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory setup where components are added in sequence assembles goods systematically.

clue.text: Wellington's damned book-maker?

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, threatened with exposure in memoirs, retorted 'Publish and be damned', so the book's issuer is the one damned

explanation.surface: A bookie cursed by the Iron Duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book-maker' suggests a bookie, but means whoever issues books.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that issues books is literally a maker of books for sale.

clue.text: Concern of an eleven yet to be organised

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a team of eleven in cricket

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worry for a cricket team still not sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be organised' turns YET into ETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Worry and unease are a state of concern.

clue.text: Battle contributing to military prestige

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A battle that added to an army's prestige.
explanation.walkthrough: Ypres, in Belgium, was the scene of several First World War battles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flanders town gives its name to several First World War battles.

clue.text: Forming an impression of a person with convictions

definitions.text: Forming an impression of a person with convictions

parts.words: Forming an impression of a person with convictions
parts.note: sounds like judging someone's principled character, but means police taking inky marks from a criminal's fingertips

explanation.surface: Sizing up someone of strong principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' is a physical print and 'convictions' are criminal ones, not beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Police record a convicted person's fingertip marks in ink.

clue.text: Noticing nothing unusual in disguise

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the preceding word arranged in an unexpected way

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone noticing nothing odd about a person in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges NOTICING into INCOGNIT, then O for nothing ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling under a concealed identity is being in disguise.

clue.text: He may stand up for another's rights

definitions.text: He may stand up for another's rights

parts.words: He may stand up for another's rights
parts.note: reads like a civil-liberties champion, but describes a fighter who stays on his feet to take an opponent's punches with the right hand

explanation.surface: A champion of other people's civil rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rights' are right-handed punches, and 'stand up for' means stand up to face them in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizefighter stands up against an opponent's right-hand blows.

clue.text: It was used to make the link at Gretna Green

definitions.text: It was used to make the link at Gretna Green

parts.words: It was used to make the link at Gretna Green
parts.note: a blacksmith's workshop, where eloping couples were famously married over the anvil, and where metal links are made

explanation.surface: How eloping couples tied the knot at the famous Scottish border village.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was where runaway English couples married, the blacksmith officiating at his anvil; 'link' is both the marriage and a chain link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy's hearth heats iron for chain links, and the Gretna smithy hosted weddings.

clue.text: Ostentation of gold in complicated designs

indicators.note: in places the gold symbol within the rearranged letters
complicated means made intricate, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Showiness from gold woven into intricate patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' gives GDINESS, and 'in' splits it after the first letter to take the gold symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish showiness and flashy display amount to vulgar ostentation.

clue.text: Residential period, a requirement to complete the course

definitions.text: a requirement to complete the course

parts.note: home is where one resides
a stretch is a period of time, especially a prison term

explanation.surface: A spell living in, needed to finish a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a racecourse, not a programme of study.
explanation.definitionFit: The final straight before the finishing post must be run to finish a race.

clue.text: Ships often crossing the bar

definitions.meaning: large glasses for sherry or beer are often handed across a pub bar

explanation.definitionFit: Two-masted sailing vessels share their name with tall drinking glasses served in pubs.

clue.text: Complain thus about wages

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for wages is read backwards

parts.note: pay means wages

explanation.surface: Workers grumbling over their pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag and grumble shrilly is informal speech for complaining.

clue.text: Enjoyed being under the influence

definitions.meaning: had the benefit of, as in enjoyed good health
controlled by a spirit or demon

explanation.definitionFit: Owned or had the use of something, and also gripped by a demon.

clue.text: Rigid form of worship

parts.note: sounds like a strict liturgy, but a form is also a bench, and this is a hard church bench

explanation.surface: A strict, unbending liturgy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'form' is a backless bench, as in old school forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A church seat in rows for the congregation is a stiff wooden bench used at services.

clue.text: Serving up uncooked food results in hostility

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: raw means uncooked
fare is food

explanation.surface: Serving raw food causes a row with diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving up' reverses RAW to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is open hostility.

clue.text: Charge for port nurse used to get drunk

parts.note: to nurse a grudge is to harbour it

indicators.note: getting drunk leaves one unsteady, so these letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse made drunk on a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is a harbour, not the wine; 'get drunk' turns USED into DUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships pay fees for berthing and using a haven's facilities.

clue.text: All by oneself, helpless?

definitions.meaning: read literally as without help, not as powerless

explanation.definitionFit: Doing it without assistance, and literally lacking help.

clue.text: Sort of carrier for staff of office?

definitions.meaning: an armoured vehicle for troops is a ... carrier
the employees of an office, punning on a staff as a ceremonial rod of office

explanation.definitionFit: Employees taken together are an organisation's staff, and the word also names a military troop carrier.

clue.text: Money belt

definitions.meaning: to belt is to hit hard

explanation.definitionFit: The British currency unit, and to hammer someone with blows.

clue.text: Box kite

definitions.meaning: slang for an old aeroplane, like kite in RAF slang

explanation.definitionFit: A slatted packing case is a box, and old pilots' slang used the word for a rickety aircraft.

clue.text: Revolutionary firm about belief

indicators.note: about means the company abbreviation surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a Red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A radical company with a set of convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the piece RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith or creed sets out what someone believes.

clue.text: States the time for practice

parts.note: the States is the US
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: America sets the time for a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary use, as in established linguistic custom, is practice.

clue.text: Suggestions disruption of unions is about to finish

indicators.note: is about means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
disruption breaks the letters of the word up into a new order

parts.note: to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Hints that trade-union unrest is about to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption of' gives INNUOS; 'is about' means it wraps round the word for finish, splitting after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Veiled hints and insinuations are suggestions made indirectly.

clue.text: Equestrian discipline is a habit that comes with time

indicators.note: comes with places one piece directly beside the next

parts.note: a habit is a garment, a dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A riding style that becomes a habit over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a routine, but it is clothing, as in a riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Training a horse to perform precise movements is a competitive riding sport.

clue.text: Rich enough to have the power to fire

definitions.text: to have the power to fire
definitions.meaning: of a gun, charged with ammunition and ready to shoot

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for wealthy, and a gun charged with cartridges is ready to shoot.
